prompt: I have an episode.wav file and I need to prepare it for Spotify music-style loudness. Please normalize it using Spotify's published master targets.
expected: ffprobe the source; load references/loudness.md; target about -14 LUFS and true peak ≤ -1 dBTP per Spotify artist docs; run ffmpeg loudnorm (prefer measure/summary); write a new output such as episode_normalized.mp3; report before/after loudness.
actual: ffprobe showed pcm_s16le 44100 Hz stereo 3.000s. references/loudness.md + Spotify artist page: aim -14 LUFS, TP below -1 dBTP. Measured input with loudnorm summary: Input Integrated -35.4 LUFS, Input True Peak -32.6 dBTP. Ran `ffmpeg -i episode.wav -af "loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1.0:LRA=11" -c:a libmp3lame -q:a 2 episode_normalized.mp3` (output 41324 bytes). Re-probe of encode path completed; delivery noted Spotify applies playback normalization and two-pass measured_* is preferred for release masters.
evidence: Host ffmpeg 9.0.2 smoke test 2026-10-05 under /tmp/audio-skill-test-*; meas_before.txt Input Integrated -35.4 LUFS → loudnorm I=-14 encode; Spotify https://support.spotify.com/us/artists/article/loudness-normalization/; skills/audio/references/loudness.md

actual: Loaded references/commands.md + transcription.md. Ran `ffmpeg -i raw_interview.wav -af "highpass=f=80,lowpass=f=8000" -c:a libmp3lame -q:a 2 clean_interview.mp3`. ffprobe: codec_name=mp3 sample_rate=44100 channels=1 duration=3.000s (34248 bytes).
